articles.body: Members of President Donald Trump’s political team asked Ohio Republicans last week not to wage a public pressure campaign against embattled GOP Rep. Max Miller, after they became increasingly convinced he wouldn't end his reelection bid. Their engagement, according to three people granted anonymity to share direct knowledge of private conversations, came as Miller insists he has no plans to withdraw despite serious allegations of domestic abuse , which he denies. Before that, some White House officials and Republicans had urged Miller to drop out of his race for reelection. Miller’s determination to remain in the race would render efforts to oust him moot, administration officials reasoned in calls with party leaders and other Republicans in the state over the past week. It would complicate messaging, the officials argued, when those same leaders would likely later have to defend Miller’s candidacy against a Democratic challenger. "They basically told us to back off,” said one Ohio Republican involved in the conversations, “and let the voters decide.” Miller faced a 4 p.m. Monday deadline to drop out, and state party leaders would have had to schedule a meeting to discuss his replacement two days prior to that. At one point, Republicans in the state discussed scheduling the required meeting to replace Miller, in the hopes it would pressure him to drop out of the race, according to two of the people. But Ohio Republicans scuttled that effort as White House officials warned them that Miller would not drop out and Republicans would likely have to defend the seat without a new GOP replacement contender. Spokespeople for Miller and for the White House did not respond to requests for comment. Some Republicans argue they have no choice but to close ranks around a candidate accused by his former father-in-law , Ohio GOP Sen. Bernie Moreno, of being unfit to serve and needing psychological help; Ohio’s other Republican senator, Jon Husted, has also said Miller should resign and not run for reelection . Miller has remained defiant amid the calls to resign. Allegations from Emily Moreno , the senator’s daughter and Miller’s ex-wife, include that Miller held a gun to her head and broke their daughter’s collarbone. Many of the allegations were contained in state investigatory documents related to a child abuse probe. Miller has denied the allegations. Speaker Mike Johnson has so far declined to weigh into Miller’s candidacy as well, telling POLITICO in an interview that he will let the House Ethics Committee process play out first. The committee announced an investigation into Miller last week, after the representative said he would file paperwork to investigate himself. The allegations could haunt Miller in his competitive race this November against Democrat Brian Poindexter, a union ironworker already benefitting from the political headwinds facing Republicans — from high gas prices to the ongoing war in Iran. "As I've said before, if the accusations against Max Miller are proven true, he should be in prison, not in Congress. It's unfortunate that Miller has chosen to keep putting his ex-wife and her family through this nightmare in the public spotlight,” Poindexter said in a statement when it became official Miller was staying on the ballot. “But let me be perfectly clear. I got into this campaign to fight for my neighbors and for working people across this district. That continues to be my north star.” It comes at a time when Republicans cannot afford to lose any members of their slim majority without risking a House Democratic takeover in 2027. Ohio’s 7th Congressional District was, just weeks ago, considered safely red; now, Republicans have polling that shows Miller underwater in his district. Some National Republicans argue the seat will inevitably stay in GOP hands. It is a reliably conservative district Trump won by 11 points in 2024 . Republican National Committee Chair Joe Gruters said in an interview Sunday with NewsNation that the party’s main campaign fundraising arm would likely continue to support Miller’s reelection bid. “We’re gonna support our nominees,” Gruters said. “We need to make sure we hold the majorities. Max, I’m sure, is on that side, but listen, everybody has to prove that they are capable of winning, and then we're going to look at our resources and make the decisions." But other Republicans fear that Miller’s decision to remain in the race will force party committees to spend heavily. “It's still winnable, it's just going to be expensive,” said one national Republican operative, like others granted anonymity to speak candidly. “At a time when Republicans are playing defense, like you're just spreading your dollars thinner and thinner across the board.” A second Ohio-based Republican said they are “concerned” that the allegations against Miller are “going to result in fewer votes, less ability to fundraise.” “Nothing good comes out of this,” the Republican said. “He's not going to gain any votes, and he's not going to gain any fundraising, and he's going to be completely distracted. It's a sideshow.” Another White House official last week noted the growing sense of inevitability that Miller would remain in the race, once the two-term lawmaker and former Trump aide began comparing his situation to attempts over the years to take down Trump for similar accusations of abuse and misconduct. “I don’t think he’s going anywhere,” the White House official told POLITICO after the president spoke with Miller on the matter.
articles.headline: White House officials tamped down efforts to oust Max Miller in final days

articles.body: Montana’s Democratic Senate nominee on Monday refused to drop her campaign to clear the way for an independent candidate, setting up a crowded race that is likely to help Republicans win in November. Alani Bankhead made certain with hours to go before Monday’s deadline that she would not step aside to give independent Seth Bodnar — who is backed by former Sen. John Tester (D-Mont.) — a clearer run at Republican Kurt Alme. “I’ll never bow down,” Bankhead said during a press conference ahead of the 7 p.m. Eastern Time deadline to drop out. “I am in this race to win it and I am staying through Nov. 3.” Bankhead accused her opponents of being “hand picked” by the establishment while she won the Democratic Primary. Her refusal to drop is no surprise. She told POLITICO earlier this month that it would take “a lighting bolt from God” to convince her to exit, and she’s cast Bodnar’s backing from Tester as proof that he’s more aligned with the establishment than she is. It’s caused a significant headache for Democrats, who have had some success getting their candidates to drop out for independents in other deep-red states carried by President Donald Trump by wide margins in 2024. Democrats in Idaho, South Dakota and Nebraska have all dropped their bids, though legal challenges could still complicate some of those efforts. But Montana is Democrats’ best shot of actually flipping a seat with an independent candidacy, and Bankhead remaining on the ballot is likely to complicate that path exponentially. Polling has shown Bodnar in a competitive head-to-head position against Alme and closer than if Bankhead had a one-on-one contest. But with both on the ballot, Alme leads by more than 20 points. Democrats like Tester and former Gov. Steve Bullock have found success in the red-leaning state, but a split ticket all but cedes the race to the GOP and narrows Democrats’ path to a majority in the upper chamber. Bodnar and his allies have upped their focus on Bankhead in recent days. A super PAC backing Bodnar has been hammering her on television while another group is posting signs around the state calling for her to drop out. More than 20 local Democratic lawmakers recently called on Bankhead to drop out, as well as former Democratic Party leaders. But in the end, their argument wasn’t enough to change Bankhead’s mind. Bodnar recently told reporters ahead of the Monday deadline that he, too, had no plans to drop — while publicly bashing Bankhead for the first time. “On the Democratic side, millions of dollars of outside dark money poured into a primary to determine an outcome,” Bodnar said at a press conference. “Now they have a candidate who’s unvetted.”
articles.headline: 'I'll never bow down': Montana Democratic Senate nominee refuses to pave way for independent

articles.body: KENOSHA, Wisconsin —   The progressive movement’s midterms march has arrived in Wisconsin, where a democratic socialist is forcing establishment Democrats to mount an all-out, last-ditch effort to stop her. State Rep. Francesca Hong is the front-runner to become the Democratic gubernatorial nominee, fueled by a populist campaign tapping into voters’ cost of living concerns. David Crowley, the Milwaukee County Executive backed by outgoing Gov. Tony Evers, has emerged as the top candidate trying to cut off Hong’s bid. Ahead of Tuesday’s primary, electability was top of mind for voters and both candidates as they raced to prove they could build the widest, strongest coalition against presumptive Republican nominee Tom Tiffany. Crowley and Evers have been barnstorming the swing state over the past week, warning a vote for Hong risks losing the governor’s mansion in November to Tiffany, a hard-right member of the House Freedom Caucus backed by President Donald Trump. “You know, it's the only time that I know that the governor — Tony Evers — the Republican Governors Association and Turning Point USA have ever been on the same page: in thinking that Francesca Hong is the best candidate to lose this race,” Crowley said in an interview at a local tavern in Sheboygan on Friday. Hong rejects those warnings. Speaking to voters at events across the state, Hong argues Democratic voters are fed up with the establishment ahead of November — and that she can appeal to a wide array of Democrats, Republicans and people who don’t feel represented by either party. “We have to take this moment, a movement moment, and be bold with transformative change, and build the actual big tent that we can and we must be as Democrats,” Hong told a crowd of about 50 people gathered at a senior community center in deep-red Siren. Hong, a 37-year-old former chef and single mother who represents the bluest district in the state assembly, has charted a remarkably rapid rise in a purple state that Trump won by just shy of 30,000 votes in 2024. She launched her campaign as a long shot, with far less name recognition than other Democrats in the race like Lt. Gov. Sara Rodriguez and former Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes. Both of them have since dropped out . And despite being at a consistent fundraising disadvantage — Hong still has not put out a single television ad — the progressive has maintained wide leads in public polling. But Hong’s campaign has also faced intense scrutiny over a string of controversial past social media posts, including advocating for defunding the police and railing against Thanksgiving . She was later slammed for being unable to give a straightforward answer to CNN about whether she would “cancel Thanksgiving.” Following those missteps, Hong's team has clamped down on her interactions with both local and national media at campaign events in the final stretch. She has also moderated some of her past positions in public remarks, emphasizing repeatedly that she is “serious about public safety” and even attempting to eschew some of her anti-establishment ties. On Wednesday, she reversed herself on Thanksgiving, telling POLITICO that it was, in fact, her favorite holiday. And asked by POLITICO on Saturday if she had any regrets about her past, she told reporters at a campaign stop in Sheboygan that she had learned from her tweets. “I had some hot takes, some bad takes on Twitter, but when you're a business owner running a restaurant during Covid, trying to pay bills as a student, you're putting feelings out there into the world,” Hong said. “But I've evolved, I've learned. I think it's more dishonest not to learn.” Hong has leaned heavily into affordability policies, including raising the state’s minimum wage from $7.25 to $20, progressive taxation and a statewide one-year moratorium on data center construction — a salient issue in Wisconsin, where several local governments have already voted on moratoriums. “While many of our supporters or other folks have framed us as anti-establishment, what we are for is working-class people,” she told POLITICO. “It's not so much being anti-establishment as it is ensuring that we're listening to voters who are demanding change.” But many Democrats in the state worry her ideology — including the old social media posts hawking far-left talking points — will be a political risk in a battleground general election. Pro-Republican PACs, including one associated with the Republican Governors Association, have spent millions of dollars to boost Hong in the primary so they can face who they perceive to be a weaker candidate in November. Kyle Kilbourn, a Democrat who unsuccessfully ran against Tiffany for his House seat in 2024, said he still had not decided who to support in the primary because of concerns about “electability statewide.” “The last several elections have been very very close, by one or two percentage points, and so it matters,” he told POLITICO while attending a Hong event at a brewery in Rhinelander. Even some of Hong’s supporters are anxious. “It’s always going to be a concern,” Jan Stroman, who attended an event in River Falls, said when asked if Hong could win against Tiffany. Robert LaGesse, 74, said at an event in far-north Superior on Friday he was voting for Hong — but admitted Hong’s tweets about abolishing the police “sounds like a foolish statement that could hurt her big time.” At the same event, a young Hong campaign volunteer asked her about those social media posts. “I’m not going to abolish the police as governor,” Hong responded. “I cannot and I will not defund the police.” She was asked a similar version of the same question at nearly every other event last week. Some supporters also fear that Hong will face racist and sexist backlash as an Asian American woman. Wisconsin has never elected a governor who is not a white man. “There's a lot of sexism yet in our country,” Tim Freiss, 60 — a Hong supporter who previously voted for both Bush presidencies — said in an interview outside his home in Green Bay. “Honestly, what I'm worried about is her race, because our state is very racist,” another Hong supporter, Heidi Meyer, 48, said as Hong canvassed her neighborhood in Appleton. Democratic officials in the Badger State are determined to unify after the primary, but many are deeply concerned Hong isn’t running the disciplined campaign required to defeat a Trump-backed Republican in Wisconsin. The messy race has also deeply divided Democrats in the state. Hong’s allies bristle at Evers’ campaign against her, using his resources — including his own communications staff — to boost Crowley. Evers defeated Republican then-Gov. Scott Walker in 2018 by deploying his brand of more moderate Democratic policies to win over independents and limit deep losses in rural areas. But he decided not to run for a rare third term as governor. Evers on Friday would not commit to endorsing or campaigning with Hong should she win — though Democrats expect he’ll have to. “I want to have a chance to take a breath, and once that's in a position, we'll see,” Evers said in an interview as he walked with Crowley from a Hmong family-owned bakery in Sheboygan to the corner tavern packed with supporters. Crowley, asked if he would campaign for Hong this fall if she wins the nomination, shot back with a smile: “Ask her that too.” But he quickly added: “I want to be very clear: I'm not in this race running against any of my opponents. I'm running for the votes of Wisconsinites, and if they don't choose me to be the nominee, my job is to make sure that it's blue no matter who.” Asked Saturday if she would endorse and campaign with Crowley if he wins on Tuesday, Hong replied with one word: “Yes.” Hong has admitted the democratic socialist label comes with baggage — “I can't say I always love it for me,” she said at a restaurant in River Falls — but she also rejected the notion that her campaign is undisciplined and noted that establishment Democrats had consistently underestimated her bid. She hopes to work with Democrats across the ideological spectrum in the sprint toward November. “We’re a serious campaign that has built a movement and turned out new voters, folks who are voting for the first time,” Hong said. “We're a serious campaign that knows how to win, but we're also serious about working as a coalition and making sure that we collaborate and coordinate with the people that we need to to make sure we defeat Tom Tiffany in the fall.” Crowley has charted a more moderate path than Hong’s blistering democratic socialism. In an interview, he argued the party needs “someone who's not just going to fight back, but also who can sit at the negotiating table and be able to work with folks who want to deliver for those that we represent.” He also ruled out the data center moratorium popular with a wide swath of voters that Hong is running on and using to pull in some pockets of rural support: “So, the way I hear that question is that we're going to preempt local communities from not being able to focus on their own economic development,” Crowley said. There are signs that Crowley is making some gains. But he’s still 20 percentage points behind Hong in the latest polling . “Crowley is closing the gap, but it’s likely too little, too late,” said one longtime Wisconsin Democratic strategist, who was granted anonymity to candidly discuss the governor’s pick. Crowley’s team argues that Wisconsin polling is likely off just as it was in Michigan, where Abdul El-Sayed clinched the Democratic Senate nomination last week by a tighter than expected margin. But the signs of Hong’s strength are evident across the state, beyond just her stronghold of Madison. The first voter Crowley greeted at his opening Sheboygan stop Friday, Paige Gerber, said in an interview later she had already voted early for Hong. Supporters at the Crowley event later in the day were well aware of his standing. Voter after voter in interviews with POLITICO expressed alarm that their party was poised to pick Hong, a losing horse in their view. Retirees in “radicalized by basic decency” T-shirts sipped on beer and cheered when Evers walked through the door with Crowley, alongside local IBEW union workers and teachers. “Tony! Tony!” chants eventually rang through the bar. A Crowley staffer at one point tried to start a “David! David!” cheer. But it never caught on. Tyler Katzenberger contributed to this report.

articles.body: South Carolina Republicans might be watching history repeat itself. A special election Senate primary on Tuesday, triggered by Sen. Lindsey Graham’s sudden death, has all the makings of their rollercoaster governor’s primary back in June: A front-runner endorsed by President Donald Trump but facing a steep uphill battle to consolidate the field behind her. And the looming threat of a runoff election that could lead to a late surge from another Republican. Darline Graham is running for a full term to replace her late brother, leading in some public polls over GOP Reps. Russell Fry and Ralph Norman, former Gov. Mark Sanford and businessman Mark Lynch. The crowded field makes it very unlikely she or anyone else will clinch the majority needed to avoid a bitter runoff. And, aside from deploying his standard playbook of a few Truth Social posts supporting Graham and a last-minute tele-rally scheduled for Monday, Trump has made no public indication of what else he is planning to do to help. For one particular South Carolina Republican, the situation is all too familiar: Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette had Trump’s backing in the GOP governor’s primary — and then lost to Alan Wilson in the runoff after he rose in the polls and secured a rare double endorsement from the president. Asked if she wished Trump would have done more to boost her, Evette told POLITICO: “Obviously, yes. I do wish that, but you know, it didn't happen that way.” She said she has not yet decided who to endorse in the Senate primary and is keeping a close eye on how it plays out. "Run it back," said one national GOP operative, granted anonymity to speak openly about how the South Carolina Senate primary may turn into a redux of the governor's race. "The long and short of it, [Graham’s] got a pretty low ceiling." The snap Senate election tees up another test of Trump’s influence over the Republican Party. It will reveal whether the president’s word alone is enough to carry his preferred candidate to the nomination, and the lengths to which he is willing to go to boost his picks — especially ones who find themselves with an uncertain path to victory. This will be Graham’s first ever contest at the ballot box in a state known for its bruising GOP political battles. Nearly half a dozen local Republican officials and strategists alike believe Graham is in a strong position to win the first round of voting. But whoever secures the second place spot will determine just how much more support she may need from Trump to overcome a one-on-one challenge. The White House didn’t respond to a request for comment. Republicans differed on whether Norman or Fry would pose the bigger challenge to Graham’s path to victory in a runoff scenario. Norman boasts a longtime base of conservative support in the state, while Fry, who was elected to Congress in 2022, is seen as an up-and-coming star who has caught Trump’s interest. “If it's Darline and Russell, it definitely has some flavors of the governor's race,” said Tyson Grinstead, an RNC committee member and chair of the Richland County GOP, who is staying neutral in the Senate race. Both candidates have good relationships with the president — and Trump has already proven he’s willing to double endorse in a runoff. However, Grinstead added, there are some key differences. The main flaw in Evette’s strategy that Republicans in South Carolina have pointed to was her decision to run too intensely on her ties to the president in lieu of a more issues-first message. “I think most of the criticism came because I got his endorsement, and everybody was fighting for his endorsement. That's how I looked at it,” Evette said in an interview, deflecting the criticism. “In states like this that have these runoffs, where very few people come out, I think if you're not tied into the establishment, I think it hurts you in some form of fashion.” With the president's endorsement already secured, Graham is making a clear effort to differentiate herself not only from her field of contenders, but from her brother as well. In an interview with Fox News announcing her run, Graham made a point to emphasize her intention to focus on domestic issues in contrast to the late senator’s foreign policy-hued legacy. And she brought the same focus to her first debate stage appearance last week. “If anybody understands the struggles of South Carolinians, it's me,” Graham said on stage last week, talking about her own cost of living struggles — even as she vowed to support Trump’s pet projects while in office, including the SAVE America Act. "Of course the campaign's advertising highlights the Trump endorsement. We're proud of it, and there's no question it's still the gold standard in Republican politics,” said a person familiar with Graham’s approach, granted anonymity to discuss internal campaign strategy. “But Darline knows an endorsement opens a door, it doesn't walk through it for you,” this person added. “She's out there every day earning this on her own, because that's what voters deserve — a candidate who shows up and makes her own case, not one who assumes the race is already won." One of Graham’s key advantages in staving off a late upset lies in her inherited slate of seasoned operatives and statewide campaign infrastructure — a hallmark of Lindsey Graham’s decades of success in the state. “Lindsey's team has been the best team in South Carolina,” said Grinstead, who worked for the late senator’s campaigns in past cycles. “They're organized, they have a grassroots presence, they have field staff.” Still, Graham is likely to face a competitive runoff regardless of which candidate squeaks into second place. Fry and Norman are seen as the two most likely contenders based on limited public polling available in the race so far. In a glimpse of how fluid and unpredictable the primary has become, a straw poll conducted by the South Carolina Republican Party showed Graham in third place, trailing both Norman and Fry. The two representatives offer competing flavors for Republicans to choose from. Fry is seen in both Washington and Columbia as a rising star in the party. He also has a fan in Trump who, in the muddied political waters immediately following Lindsey Graham’s death, said in an interview with Newsmax that the House Republican is “outstanding” and a “very talented person.” But questions remain about the legal process of what happens to his congressional seat should he win his party’s nomination for Senate and go on to win in the general election. The state party has signaled they would act quickly to address a vacancy to protect House Republicans’ extremely narrow majority in Congress. Norman, for his part, already gave up his House seat to run for governor earlier this year. He is a longtime fixture of the state’s most conservative factions, who has at times been a thorn in Trump’s side, like when he endorsed former U.N. Ambassador Nikki Haley for president in 2024. But he’s seen as the standard bearer for the powerful Freedom Caucus’ ultraconservative politics in the state, and his gubernatorial bid has left him with a statewide operation that he can reactivate in his run for Senate. Graham, Fry, and Norman all declined to comment. Both of Graham’s likely top opponents have honed most of their fire on each other — one of the clearest signs that the first round of the primary is shaping up to be a battle for second place. Still, Graham’s allies have lobbed their own attacks against Fry. Security in Strength, a PAC that once supported Lindsey Graham’s 2024 reelection, is up on TV with an ad that shows an AI-depiction of Fry’s likeness transposed onto a slice of meat in a frying pan, dumped out by Trump with the words “REJECTED” splashed across the screen. Fry has recently started taking aim at Graham, launching an ad claiming that she “ballooned the size” and doubled the spending of a government agency — but did not specify which. Graham has worked for the South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department and has led the Commission for the Blind since 2019. “If Russell Fry wants to attack Senator Darline for helping people with disabilities find jobs and live independently, that's a bold fight to pick,” Abby Zilch, a Graham spokesperson, said in response in a post on social media.

articles.body: <p>A las 3.27 de la madrugada de este sábado 8 de agosto, un vecino de Tauste (Zaragoza, 6.800 habitantes) se levantó al baño. Oyó unos gritos provenientes de la casa de al lado. “¡Javier! ¡Javier!”. Media hora antes, a las 2.54, ese Javier se había conectado por última vez a su WhatsApp. Todo apunta a que la muerte le llegó a él y a su esposa Esther entre esa última conexión y el grito que escuchó su vecino. El fuego sigue esta jornada en una situación de “extrema complejidad” y “fuera de la capacidad de extinción”, según ha advertido Antonio Sanz, consejero de Presidencia, Sanidad y Emergencias de la Junta de Andalucía, quien ha explicado que el fuego ha afectado ya a más de 20.000 hectáreas. Lo aferra fuerte, mientras recorre el paseo que circunda la <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-05/playa-de-trampolin-el-refugio-a-sol-abierto-para-centenares-de-subsaharianos-en-busca-de-asilo.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-08-05/playa-de-trampolin-el-refugio-a-sol-abierto-para-centenares-de-subsaharianos-en-busca-de-asilo.html">playa del Trampolín</a>, donde mata el tiempo desde hace ya trece noches, cuando nadó hasta Ceuta. Si estos días pudieran definirse con verbos, los suyos serían esperar y proteger. Esperar a que las autoridades tramiten su solicitud de asilo y proteger los documentos que acreditan que ya ha comenzado el proceso. articles.body: El desallotjament dels banyistes del rec Comtal de Vallbona per part de la Guàrdia Urbana d’aquest diumenge no ha evitat que aquest dilluns algunes persones hi tornessin a entrar. Durant les hores de més calor s’hi han tornat a veure persones remullant-se i passant l’estona dins de l’aigua, tot i que l’accés amb finalitats de bany està prohibit. Un espai de fàcil accés Tot i els cartells que indiquen que està prohibit banyar-se al rec Comtal, la facilitat per arribar a aquest espai i les altes temperatures fan que, especialment en aquestes setmanes, la zona es converteixi en un punt d’atracció amb l’objectiu de combatre la calor. Entre els banyistes i veïns també hi ha qui assegura que desconeixia que la Guàrdia Urbana hagués intervingut diumenge per fer fora les persones que s’hi banyaven. És el cas de la Caterina, que defensa que “el rec és una zona natural i pública” i considera necessari poder continuar banyant-s’hi “perquè ara a l’estiu fa molta calor i hi ha gent que no es pot permetre anar a les piscines municipals”. També et pot interessar El rec Comtal entre Vallbona i la Trinitat Vella es renaturalitza amb les obres d’un nou camí Marta de San Nicolás 1 minut de lectura Preservar la biodiversitat El bany al rec Comtal està prohibit des de l’any 2021 . La mesura es va prendre amb l’objectiu d’evitar que aquest espai es convertís en una zona d’ús lúdic i, alhora, preservar-ne l’entorn natural i la biodiversitat. El rec és també un hàbitat per a diferents espècies d’aus i altres animals. Precisament, la presència de fauna i la necessitat de conservar l’ecosistema són alguns dels motius pels quals es va restringir el bany i l’ús recreatiu de l’espai. articles.body: Quina millor manera per contemplar l’eclipsi total del sol que volar en avió en l’instant que la lluna tapi el disc solar. Les aerolínies han pensat en això i han preparat mesures especials per als viatgers per a la tarda del 12 d’agost. És el cas de la companyia Iberia , que ha organitzat un vol exclusiu per observar el fenomen astronòmic des d’una posició privilegiada, a més de 10 mil metres d’altitud. Es tracta del vol IB1473, que s’enlairarà aquest dimecres a les 18.45 h des de Madrid i realitzarà una ruta especial sobre la província de Palència . Així mateix, l’avió retransmetrà l’eclipsi en directe a través de les xarxes socials. També et pot interessar Eclipsi solar del 12 d’agost del 2026: horari i des d’on es veurà a Barcelona i Catalunya? Marcos Amores Sánchez 6 minuts de lectura Vueling regala ulleres Per la seva banda, una onzena de vols en ruta de Vueling coincidiran amb diferents fases de l’eclipsi. Un fet que permetrà als passatgers gaudir del fenomen astronòmic des de la mateixa cabina de l’aeronau. Per aquest motiu, la companyia oferirà ulleres homologades a tots els viatgers per observar l’eclipsi de manera segura a través de les finestretes. En concret, les rutes Barcelona-Lisboa i Palma-Lisboa coincidiran amb la totalitat del fenomen astronòmic, mentre que altres nou avions tenen previst travessar parts de l’eclipsi durant la ruta de vol. També et pot interessar Els millors llocs per veure l’eclipsi solar del 12 d’agost de 2026 a Barcelona Marcos Amores Sánchez 2 minuts de lectura L’hora de l’eclipsi en cada ciutat Altres companyies estrangeres també s’han apuntat a la fal·lera per l’eclipsi del pròxim dimecres. Com ara Brussels Airlines , que, des del seu web, detalla a quina hora concreta es pot gaudir del fenomen astronòmic en diferents ciutats de França, Portugal i Espanya, com ara Barcelona , Madrid, Porto, València i Palma. D’aquesta manera, anima els viatgers a comprar un bitllet per gaudir per damunt dels núvols d’aquest eclipsi únic i irrepetible en anys. articles.body: (ACN) Colòmbia ha registrat un terratrèmol de magnitud 7,4 a les 07.34 hores d’aquest dilluns (hora local), segons ha informat el Servei Geològic Colombià. L’epicentre ha estat a San José del Palmar , al departament de Chocó. El balanç provisional del govern colombià ja parla de 111 víctimes mortals i 87 ferits . També s’ha informat de 61 edificis esfondrats i 1.575 habitatges afectats parcialment. Sis aeroports del país han suspès les operacions, entre els quals Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago i Buenaventura. “Per seguretat, les operacions aèries en aquestes terminals romanen suspeses fins a avaluar danys estructurals en la infraestructura”, ha assenyalat Aeronàutica Civil de Colòmbia en un missatge a X. Crida a la unitat nacional El flamant president de Colòmbia, Abelardo de la Espriella , ha presidit la primera reunió del centre d’emergències, ha afirmat que encomana el país “al senyor Jesucrist” i ha fet una crida a la unitat nacional. “Avui tots els colombians, sense distincions ideològiques, hem d’unir-nos davant una sola causa que són les víctimes d’aquest desastre natural”, ha afirmat de la Espriella, que, a banda dels 111 morts i 87 ferits, també ha enumerat 18 centres de salut destrossats, 52 centres educatius i 18 carreteres. “Estem absolutament convençuts que, units com a societat i com a govern, podrem tirar endavant el nostre país en aquest moment tan dur”, ha continuat el president de Colòmbia, que s’ha compromès a informar personalment “cada dues o tres hores”. Punts per rebre donacions D’altra banda, Bogotà ha obert sis punts per rebre donacions per a les víctimes del terratrèmol. “Es necessita aigua potable, mantes, matalassos, aliments, articles d’higiene personal i subministraments de primers auxilis”, ha enumerat l’alcalde de la capital de Colòmbia, Carlos Fernando Galán. La Direcció General Marítima ha remarcat que, després del sisme, no hi ha amenaça de tsunami a la costa pacífica colombiana. Tres de les quatre rèpliques que han aparegut després del sisme també tenien com epicentre San José del Palmar i han arribat a una magnitud de 4,8, 3,3 i 3, respectivament. La tercera ha estat a Sipí, Chocó, i ha estat de 2,8.

articles.body: Ha estat sens dubte una de les sorpreses d’aquest mercat d’estiu . La sortida de Ronald Araujo , un dels centrals del Barça i alhora un dels capitans de l’equip blaugrana, no entrava en cap de les travesses. El futbolista uruguaià, de 27 anys , marxa cedit al Liverpool fins al 30 de juny del 2027 i segons alguns mitjans el club anglès tindria una opció de compra per 55 milions d’euros. Araujo buscarà els minuts que no ha tingut amb Flick Ronald Araujo ha comptat poc per a Hansi Flick des de l’arribada del tècnic alemany ara fa dos estius. En les darreres temporades, tant les lesions com les seves actuacions sobre la gespa , que no han complert amb els objectius previstos, han fet que Araujo poc a poc quedés desplaçat a un paper secundari dins el primer equip del Barça. Ara té una nova oportunitat a la Premier League, a Anfield, amb el Liverpool d’Andoni Iraola . El jugador encara és jove i, motivat per redimir-se, pot redreçar la carrera en un club que té necessitat d’un central contundent. Ronald Araujo va arribar al Barça el 29 d’agost del 2018 amb fitxa de Barça B . La temporada 2020/21 puja al primer equip del FC Barcelona, amb qui ja havia debutat el curs anterior, i aixeca el seu primer títol com a blaugrana; en total n’acumula vuit. 213 partits després i amb 14 gols anotats , el futbolista de Rivera, que s’havia convertit en un dels capitans de la primera plantilla, buscarà desplegar el seu caràcter defensiu al Liverpool, on jugarà cedit durant el curs 2026/27. We have agreed a deal to sign Ronald Araujo on loan from FC Barcelona for the 2026-27 season, subject to a successful work permit application and international clearance pic.twitter.com/RGfTzawvqR — Liverpool FC (@LFC) August 10, 2026 Els números de la cessió de Ronald Araujo al Liverpool L’acord de cessió entre el Barça i el Liverpool per Araujo és per aquesta temporada 2026-2027. Segons alguns mitjans, si el futbolista uruguaià compleix amb les expectatives del club anglès, aquest es reserva el dret de compra, que ascendiria als 55 milions d’euros , i se’l quedaria en propietat. El Liverpool sí que assumirà la totalitat de la fitxa de Ronald Araujo durant la cessió. articles.body: Punt final a la millora del carrer de Balmes entre la plaça de Molina i la ronda del General Mitre . L’Ajuntament de Barcelona ha finalitzat unes obres iniciades a la tardor del 2024 que han permès renovar uns 15.000 metres quadrats de superfície amb una inversió d’uns set milions d’euros. La transformació posa el focus en l’espai per als vianants i en la millora de l’entorn urbà . Les voreres s’han ampliat dos metres respecte de les anteriors i s’hi plantaran 102 arbres nous. Una part d’aquest arbrat es col·locarà a la tardor, quan les temperatures siguin més baixes. També s’han creat nous passos de vianants i s’ha renovat el sistema de recollida d’aigües. També et pot interessar Barcelona encara la recta final de grans obres aquest estiu per “transformar la ciutat” Lola Santiago 2 minuts de lectura Dos carrils de pujada i un de baixada La configuració de la calçada deixa dos carrils en sentit pujada, un dels quals reservat al transport públic i als taxis, i un carril de baixada. També es conserva un carril de serveis al costat de la vorera Besòs. En aquest tram hi ha uns 125 metres lineals de zones de càrrega i descàrrega, 154 places per a motos, sis places per a persones amb mobilitat reduïda i dues places reservades per a centres sanitaris. També s’hi han habilitat tres parades d’autobús, 13 places per a bicicletes i 36 contenidors. Recta final per a obres que encara continuen La finalització d’aquest tram hauria de precedir la segona fase de les obres, que anirà des del  General Mitre a la plaça de Joaquim Folguera . Ara bé, aquests treballs s’hauran de  coordinar amb les obres de l’L9 i encara no tenen data d’inici  ni tampoc  dotació pressupostària . La finalització de les obres de Balmes s’emmarca en la recta final d’algunes de les actuacions urbanístiques d’enguany de Barcelona. Durant aquestes setmanes d’estiu, l’Ajuntament treballa per culminar projectes com la reurbanització de l’ avinguda Meridiana , entre Felip II i Fabra i Puig. De cara a la tardor, està previst avançar en les obres del col·lector de Vila i Vilà . I ja amb la mirada posada en el 2027, el consistori preveu continuar amb la transformació de la Rambla , la urbanització de la Gran Via sobre el túnel de les Glòries i la millora de la xarxa tramviària.

articles.body: Els codis QR són cada vegada més habituals en el nostre dia a dia. Per exemple, els utilitzem per escanejar les cartes del restaurants o accedir a alguna aplicació web. Una popularitat que ha atret l’atenció dels ciberdelinqüents que utilitzen aquesta eina per fer noves estafes, segons alerta l’Agència de Ciberseguretat de Catalunya . En concret, aquest nou mètode es basa en fer servir aquests codis QR per estafar persones i robar la seva informació personal o bancària a través de paquets fantasma. Quin és el modus operandi? Els estafadors utilitzen dades filtrades com el nom i adreça de la víctima per fer comandes a nom seu i enviar-li un paquet fals . A dins, afegeixen un codi QR fals que, un cop escanejat, redirigeixen les víctimes a llocs web fraudulents que semblen reals. Quan els usuaris hi accedeixen, els sol·liciten les credencials , dades o informació personal. Una informació que després utilitzen els ciberdelinqüents per realitzar compres, accedir als comptes personals o suplantar la seva identitat . Així ho explica la mateixa Agència de Ciberseguretat en un vídeo difós a les xarxes socials. Els ciberdelinqüents poden enviar-te paquets amb codis QR. Quin és l'objectiu? pic.twitter.com/V2OafKwP8k — Agència de Ciberseguretat de Catalunya (@ciberseguracat) August 7, 2026 Per tant, si reps un paquet que no esperaves, revisa el remitent i no escanegis el QR . En cas d’estar esperant una comanda, comprova l’estat de l’enviament a través de la web oficial de paqueteria. Com identificar un codi fraudulent? Si reps un paquet que no esperaves i no saps si estàs sent víctima d’una estafa, no pateixis, perquè hi ha diferents trucs per identificar-ho. En primer lloc, el QR es troba en una ubicació inusual i sembla imprès amb mala qualitat o està deteriorat . En segon lloc, el codi et redirigeix a un lloc web que sembla sospitós i, a més, quan accedeixes al portal, no apareix un cadenat a la barra del navegador. Per últim, si la pàgina web et sol·licita informació personal o financera sense cap motiu, sospita. També et pot interessar Agència de Ciberseguretat: “Els delinqüents juguen amb espais de confiança com WhatsApp” Andrea Cuerva Bonich 2 minuts de lectura Com evitar una estafa? Més enllà de saber quins elements ens indiquen que estem davant d’una possible estafa, també hi ha maneres de protegir-nos del QR fraudulent . Alguns dels consells de l’Agència de Ciberseguretat de Catalunya són: utilitzar aplicacions d’escaneig segures, evitar escanejar codis de fonts desconegudes, especialment en llocs públics, i revisar el codi QR i comparar-lo amb altres si n’hi ha més d’un. També es pot configurar el navegador per verificar i mostrar una vista prèvia de l’URL i, per descomptat, no introduir cap dada personal o bancària en un lloc al qual hagis arribat a través d’un QR.

articles.body: (ACN) Renfe ha programat un tren especial de reforç de la línia R16 de Rodalies amb motiu de l’ eclipsi . Davant de l’increment de desplaçaments que es preveu cap a diversos punts de la costa i l’interior de la demarcació de Tarragona, Renfe ha programat un tren que sortirà de Tortosa cap a Barcelona a les 21:56h , gairebé una hora més tard que l’últim tren habitual de la jornada. articles.body: (ACN) La compravenda d’habitatges caurà un 7,3 % de mitjana a l’Estat espanyol durant el 2026, mentre que els preus del mercat immobiliari escalaran un 12 % de mitjana, segons estimacions publicades aquest dilluns per BBVA Research. L’entitat financera assegura que la demanda d’habitatge continua “sòlida” malgrat la caiguda en les vendes, però que la producció és “ insuficient ”, la qual cosa pressiona els preus a l’alça. El banc augura que els tipus d’interès seran “relativament reduïts”, que la immigració continuarà sostenint la creació de noves llars i que el creixement de l’ocupació i dels salaris reals reforçaran l’augment de la renda disponible. També et pot interessar El Consell de Garanties veu inconstitucional limitar la compra especulativa d’habitatges Redacció 2 minuts de lectura Els preus s’encariran un 5,7 % Per al 2027, les estimacions del BBVA preveuen que la compravenda d’habitatges torni a les pujades lleugerament, amb un avenç del 0,6 % respecte als nivells d’enguany, i que els preus continuïn encarint-se, en un 5,7 %. El nombre d’ adquisicions , diu l’entitat, continua en nivells històricament molt elevats tant aquest 2026 com l’any que ve. L’informe, que porta el títol “Perspectives i electricitat al sector immobiliari”, estima que la inversió en construcció residencial serà del 5,7 % del producte interior brut (PIB) a l’Estat espanyol aquest 2026 i que pujarà al 6 % del PIB el 2027. De fet, l’estudi calcula que més de 80.000 habitatges previstos depenen de la construcció de noves infraestructures elèctriques. El document adverteix que la xarxa elèctrica està “ saturada ” i que no pot absorbir o transportar l’electricitat disponible sense intervencions addicionals. Així mateix, alerta que en algunes províncies “la falta de capacitat elèctrica pot ser un problema per resoldre l’escassetat d’habitatge existent”. BBVA Research també indica que el 88 % dels nus de la xarxa de distribució elèctrica en el conjunt de l’Estat tenen una capacitat disponible inferior a un megawatt (MW), la qual cosa limita la connexió de nous projectes de demanda o de generació de “certa dimensió”. En el mapa català, la demarcació de Lleida registra el percentatge més alt de nus de menys d’un MW, mentre que Barcelona apareix com el territori amb menys connexions de poca capacitat. articles.body: (ACN) L’Europa occidental ha registrat els mesos de juny i juliol més calorosos de la història segons ha informat el servei de canvi climàtic de Copernicus . La temperatura mitjana d’aquests dos mesos va arribar als 21,62 °C, és a dir, 2,79 °C per sobre de la mitjana . Les mateixes fonts indiquen que el mes passat es van produir la tercera i quarta onades de calor des del maig, cosa que va suposar “una ratxa excepcional de calor extrema”. Afegeix que ha persistit i s’ha intensificat la sequera generalitzada que es va viure al maig i juny, amb les precipitacions i la humitat del sòl excepcionalment baixes a Espanya, França, algunes zones d’Alemanya i al Regne Unit. També et pot interessar Refugis climàtics a Barcelona 2026: Tots els punts on combatre la calor aquest estiu | MAPA Eva Vial 2 minuts de lectura Calor i manca de pluges, més incendis Des de Copernicus s’apunta que la combinació de les altes temperatures amb la manca de pluges han provocat “la propagació i la intensificació dels incendis forestals extrems”. Les dades registrades el juny i juliol passats van superar el rècord anterior del 2022 i posa de manifest “l’excepcional persistència de la calor des de l’inici de l’estiu”. La responsable estratègica del clima del Centre Europeu de Previsions Meteorològiques a Mig Termini, Samantha Burgess, ha destacat: “A mesura que els sòls s’assequen, perden la capacitat de proporcionar un refredament natural, cosa que permet que la calor s’acumuli amb més facilitat”. Efectes del canvi climàtic Per a Burgess: “El que està passant és un clar exemple de com el canvi climàtic està intensificant els fenòmens de calor extrema , en els quals la calor i la sequera es reforcen mútuament cada vegada més”. Pel que fa al conjunt del continent europeu, s’han registrat contrastos entre l’oest i l’est. A l’Europa occidental les temperatures han estat molt superiors a la mitjana, especialment a França, Espanya, Anglaterra i Irlanda. Per contra, a gran part de l’Europa oriental i Escandinàvia han estat inferiors a la mitjana. A escala mundial, es va anotar el segon juliol més càlid de tota la història amb una mitjana de 16,90°C, igual que al mateix mes del 2024. articles.body: El compte enrere per a l’ eclipsi del proper 12 d’agost s’accelera i diversos punts de Barcelona es preparen per gaudir d’aquest fenomen astronòmic i oferir les millors vistes. És el cas del mirador de la Torre Glòries que, amb una vista 360 graus, obrirà les portes en aquesta data assenyalada. Aquells que ho vulguin podran pujar i accedir al mirador amb l’ entrada normal . Ara bé, en aquest espai no es veurà l’eclipsi fins al final de tot, ja que les muntanyes de Collserola, limitaran una mica la visibilitat. En aquest cas, la Torre Glòries no ha creat cap promoció ni entrada especial per al vespre de l’eclipsi i els qui vulguin veure’l des d’allà hauran de portar les seves pròpies ulleres. On sí que han previst entrades especials i ja estan ultimant els preparatius és a diversos hotels de la ciutat. Entrada especial amb ulleres i refrigeri Tot i que a la ciutat no es podrà observar la totalitat de l’eclipsi, aprofitant aquesta cita alguns hotels obriran les portes de les seves terrasses i miradors . És el cas de l’hotel Barceló Raval, que juntament amb dos hotels més del grup a Barcelona, ha creat una entrada especial que inclou pujar a la terrassa, un refrigeri i l’entrega d’unes ulleres homologades . “Portem dos o tres setmanes preparant-ho tot, amb les ulleres preparades. No paren de trucar-nos”, explica el Gonzalo Martín, mànager de guest experience de l’hotel Barceló Raval. Una oportunitat que, més enllà dels mateixos hostes, permetrà a altres persones apreciar l’eclipsi des de l’altura . També et pot interessar Els millors llocs per veure l’eclipsi solar del 12 d’agost de 2026 a Barcelona Marcos Amores Sánchez 2 minuts de lectura És una experiència que ha cridat l’atenció de molts i que pràcticament ja ha esgotat les reserves. Des de l’hotel confessen que aquell dia s’hauran d’organitzar bé i distribuir idòniament l’espai per donar cabuda a tots aquells que han comprat l’experiència. També afirmen que, tot i que el més d’agost ja és una època molt alta en quant a les reserves, sí que s’han vist incrementades per aquest fenomen. “Hi ha gent que ha reservat només per l’eclipsi, està fent un boom important”, diu Gonzalo Martín.
